sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 17-02-2023 at about 8.40 a.m., the Petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LB-2792 opposite to HQTC main gate, Bellary road, near Mekhri circle,
Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50-P-8156 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) drove the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to the accident, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Baptist hospital, wherein he has taken first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Fortis hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.

It is claimed that he has spent Rs.4,50,000/- for treatment,
medicines, conveyance and other charges.

At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 63 years,
working as a Public relation officer at Sri Sai water treatment Pvt.Ltd., and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.

As the accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being insurer and owner.
3.
In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 has appeared before the court through it s counsel and filed the written statement.
The Respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court and she was placed exparte.
4. Respondent No.1- has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the alleged accident.
It has contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further, it has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle and negligence of the rider of offending vehicle in causing the accident.

It has contended that the offending vehicle was falsely implicated as the complaint was lodged after 4 days of accident and that too upon an unknown car driver and FIR was also lodged against unknown car and IMV inspection was done to the motorcycle after 15 days and IMV inspection to the car was done after 4 months of accident and as such, the offending vehicle is falsely implicated.
It has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.
On these grounds, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 17-02-2023 at about 08-40 p.m., opposite to HQTC main gate Bellary Road, Near Mekhri Circle Bengaluru, he sustained injuries Sharath Babu K S vs Kotak Mahindra General Insuarnce Co Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100528527/
2 in a road traffic accident, while he was moving on his motorcycle bearing number KA-05-LB-2792 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA -50-P-8156?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that there is violation of the policy conditions by respondent No.2 and respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

doctor is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.20.
7. On the other hand Respondent No.1 has examined its official as RW-1 and IO is examined as RW-2 and no documents have been marked.

8. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: In the Negative Issue No.3: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.4: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 17-02-2023 at about 8.40 a.m., when he was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-LB-2792 opposite to HQTC main gate, Bellary road, near Mekhri circle, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50-P-8156 drove the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to the accident, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 17.

To support of his claim, Dr.Nagaraj B.N. was examined as PW-2 and he has produced the 3 documents at Ex.P.18 to 20.
11.
It is stated that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

He has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, FIS at Ex.P.2, statement and restatement at Ex.P.3 and 4, spot mahazar at Ex.P.5, spot sketch at Ex.P.6, IMV report at Ex.P.7 & 8, Wound certificate at Ex.P.9 and charge sheet at Ex.P.10.
As per wound certificate he has sustained fracture of left clavicle and fracture dislocation of left hip.
12. The Respondent-insurance company has contended that the first information was lodged after 4 days of the incident against unknown car and FIR also registered against unknown car.

To substantiate the same,
official of the Respondent no 1 insurance company was examined as RW1 and Investigation officer was examined as RW2.
RW2 has stated that the complaint was given against unknown vehicle.
Based on CCTV footage available in the incident place, he traced out the vehicle.
During the course of cross-examination, it was suggested that no where in the charge sheet mentioning about based upon CCTV footage, he traced the offending vehicle.
He admitted the same.
He denied that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.
Except cross- examination and contention in the objections, respondent-insurance company has not produced any evidence to disprove the non involvement of offending vehicle.

Further mere failure to mention in the charge sheet that the vehicle was traced based on CCTV footage does not make it unbelievable that the offending vehicle was not involved in accident unless supported by cogent evidence.
13.
It is stated that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
In this regard Sadashivanagar traffic police registered a case in Cr.No.16/2023 for the offence punishable U/s.279 and 337 of IPC in which he has been charge sheeted.
14. In the cross-examination of PW-1 and RW2 nothing favorable to the respondent no 1 is extracted.
The Respondent no 1 has not proved the said fact by examining any eye witness or driver of the offending vehicle to support its contention with regard to non involvement of the offending vehicle.
Absolutely there are no materials to overcome the charge sheet findings and disprove the negligence driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and non involvement of offending vehicle.
Therefore, the contention raised by the Respondent no 2 holds no water.
15. There are no materials on record to disprove the Petitioner's evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondent.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
The contention raised by the respondent-insurance company holds no water.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the copy of the charge sheet is produced at Ex.P.10.charge
sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
The respondent No.1 has taken contention that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent no 1 insurance company has proved the fact that the owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.
The offending vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy, hence fastening joint liability on the Respondent no 1- insurance company.
Wherefore, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence I answer issue no.2 in the negative.

sentences.text: As per Ex.P.9 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained fracture of left clavicle and fracture dislocation of left hip.
The doctor opined that the above injuries are grievous in nature.
18. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Baptist hospital, then shifted to Fortis hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as a public relation officer at Sri Sai water treatment Pvt.Ltd., and earning a sum of .40,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
19. PW-2 Dr.Nagaraj B.N.

Orthopedic surgeon has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained left quadrilateral wall and anterior column fracture of acetabulum with left clavicle fracture in a RTA and treated at Fortis hospital, Bengaluru and underwent ORIF with 11 holed iliac plate.
He further deposed that petitioner was examined clinically and radiologically while assessing disability.

He found that Petitioner complains of pain in the left hip with numbness in the left thigh, unable to climb, sit down, squat and sit cross leg, unable to lift shoulder and restricted movements of left hip.

On examination, he has assessed the total physical disability of the left lower limb at 52%,, left upper limb at 30% and whole body physical disability at 25%.
20.
PW-2 in his cross-examination has stated that at time of discharge the condition of the petitioner was stable.
Fracture is united and injuries are healed.
he has not treated the Petitioner.
He denied that he has assessed the disability on the higher side.
It is pertinent to note that PW-2 has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

Therefore, considering that the grievous injury is on the hip and considering the difficulties and evidence of PW-2 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 8%.
21. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 63 years.

Ex.P.12 - DL shows that he was born on 10-04-1960, the same is considered as age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 63 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 7.
22.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injurt.

He was admitted in Fortis hospital,
Bengaluru.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as a public relation officer at Sri Sai water treatment Pvt.Ltd., and earning a sum of .40,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

The petitioner has produced the documents at Ex.P.13 to 16 i.e., offer letter, pay slips,
non-joining certificate and Bank statement.
Bank statement does not reveal about monthly salary of the petitioner.
The petitioner has not made any attempt to examine personal of Sri Sai water treatment Pvt.Ltd to prove the same and thereby the tribunal is considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
23. The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 16,000/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injury is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

sentences.text: Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Looking into the nature of injury, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.
Considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 8%.
Thus, loss of future income comes to Rs.16,000 x 12 x 7 x 8/100= Rs.1,07,520/- towards loss of future income.
25. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained grievous injury and was inpatient for a period of 11 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .25,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head of pain and sufferings.
26. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .20,000/- under the head of loss of amenities of life.
27. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.17 amounting to 1,09,414/-.

On perusal of final bill it appears that, the amount of Rs.69,047/- was paid out of petitioner's pocket and remaining amount was reimbursed under the Medi Assist Insurance TPA Pvt.Ltd., and he spent amount of Rs.1,09,414/- out of his pocket.
Therefore, medical bills appear to be genuine.

Hence,
Petitioner is awarded compensation of 1,09,414/- towards Medical Expenses.
28. Future medical expenses:
PW-2 has stated that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant and total hip replacement and estimated cost of surgery is Rs.4,70,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation report.
In the absence of material evidence, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses.
29. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P.20- case sheet which includes Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Fortis hospital, Bengaluru from 17- 02-2023 to 27-02-2023 i.e, for a period of 11 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .15,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
30. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Fortis hospital, Bengaluru from 17-02- 2023 to 27-02-2023 i.e, for a period of 11 days.
Considering the same around 2 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 2 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 2= 32,000/-.
31.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount No.
1. Loss of future earnings  1,07,520/-
2. Pain and Sufferings  25,000/-

32. Liability:
Respondent No.2 being the owner and the Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.

However,
Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
33. ISSUE NO.4:

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,28,934/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. (except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, the entire amount with interest shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
